tagline: A silver miners' toll road, bought for the public in 1915.
intro: From the Big Oak Flat entrance the road runs to Crane Flat, about 6,200 feet up, and turns east as the Tioga Road, a winding two-lane through lodgepole pine and red fir. It comes out onto granite at Olmsted Point, drops to Tenaya Lake, climbs again to Tuolumne Meadows and goes up through Dana Meadows to Tioga Pass at 9,945 feet. Then it falls more than 3,000 feet toward Lee Vining.

It was built in 1883 to reach silver mines east of the pass and ran as a toll road, two dollars a horse and rider. In 1915 Stephen Mather bought it, partly with his own money, and opened the high country to the public.

moments.title: Olmsted Point
moments.text: Glacial erratics lie scattered over the granite by the parking lot, and a short trail to the top of a small dome looks down Tenaya Canyon to the north side of Half Dome.

moments.title: Tenaya Lake
moments.text: Named for Chief Tenaya, who, told of the honor, said the lake already had a name, Py-we-ack. That name went to the dome east of the lake.

moments.title: Tuolumne Meadows
moments.text: A sub-alpine meadow along the Tuolumne River at about 8,600 feet, with eleven major climbing domes strung from Stately Pleasure Dome above Tenaya Lake to Lembert Dome on its east side.

practical: Tioga Pass is closed in winter, normally from about the end of October or November until late May; in heavy snow years it has stayed shut into late July.
